calibration_status: provisional, uncalibrated: constants chosen from the rounding structure of the published table and general methodological convention; no real-paper calibration in this session (corpus calibration arms unperformed).

supporting: Model 3 first-order Strategic Deviation (positive, required for an interior maximum)
F test Model 3 vs Model 2 (identification/inference diagnostic)

lower_tiers: F tests M2 vs M1, M3 vs M1 (diagnostic)
focal_structure.paper_rule: The paper outcome is the primary focal (H3, Model 3 SD^2) claim outcome, determined jointly with the Model 3 SD term as a single claim (both must meet criteria for consistent). It is qualified, not overridden, by the secondary focal and lower tiers using the scoring.md mapping: fully reproduced = primary consistent and no tier discrepant; partially reproduced = primary fragile, or primary consistent with a discrepant lower tier or secondary focal; not reproduced = primary discrepant; indeterminate/not attemptable/fragile inference reported as such. Rationale: title, abstract and conclusion state the strategic-balance (concave) result as the paper's contribution; H2 is the competing linear test.

implementation_agreement.pairing: Compare A, B, C at each origin before targets: identical sample_hash and N; coefficients agree if |diff| <= 1e-6 * max(1, |b|) and SEs likewise. A pair agrees on a spec if all four models agree. Two agreeing of three permit scoring on that pair; the third goes to code audit. No agreeing pair -> indeterminate (implementation_disagreement).
implementation_agreement.grid_agreement: Report the share of specs on which each pair agrees; never average implementations.

rounding: Published coefficient b and SE s printed to 3 decimals: intervals [b-0.0005, b+0.0005], [s-0.0005, s+0.0005]. Stars are inequalities. All comparisons use the most favourable point of the rounding interval (benefit of rounding).
sign: Sign agreement if the reconstructed estimate has the same sign as the published estimate. If the published rounding interval contains 0, sign is not assessed.

inference.mapping: *** and ** map to band p<.01; * to .01-.05; no star maps to p>=.05 (band .05-.10 or >=.10, ambiguous across those two).
inference.reconstructed_p: two-sided t p from native conventional WLS (tail unstated in article; both readers record unstated tails). One-sided p in the hypothesised direction reported alongside as the directional reading; it never converts an opposite-sign estimate into support.
inference.rule: Inference agrees if reconstructed band equals or is stronger than the published band for a positive significance claim; a one-band weakening is a difference but never sufficient for discrepancy; a two-or-more-band weakening (e.g. published p<.01, reconstructed p>=.05 with band >=.10) meets the discrepancy inference criterion. For a published non-significant term, a newly significant reconstruction (p<.05) is a contradiction.
inference.benchmark_inference: Not audited. Assignment-level clustering does not apply (observational population; both readers record assignment unit as not applicable). No alternative benchmark declared. Bank-clustered CR1 SEs are reported as a non-equivalent sensitivity only. Fragile-inference outcome therefore cannot be assigned.

magnitude.regime: different_vintage_public_reconstruction (independently rebuilt sample and variables from archived public Call Reports; not author data)
magnitude.metric: d = distance from reconstructed estimate to the published rounding interval, divided by the upper end of the published SE interval.
magnitude.relative_effect: Also report (b_rec - b_pub)/|b_pub| and the ratio; descriptive only.
magnitude.no_published_se: magnitude not audited (e.g., F statistics, SSE).

n_tolerance.use: N outside tolerance cannot by itself create discrepancy; if a claim would otherwise be discrepant while N is outside tolerance, it becomes indeterminate (source_vintage/sample_construction). A consistent claim with N outside tolerance remains consistent with an explicit coverage qualification.

claim_outcome_at_one_origin.consistent: sign agrees, inference agrees, magnitude band consistent (or not audited with reason stated)
claim_outcome_at_one_origin.grey: sign agrees, and either magnitude grey or inference one band weaker
claim_outcome_at_one_origin.discrepant_candidate: agreeing implementations; sign opposite, or inference two-or-more bands weaker, or magnitude outside

origin_ambiguity: Two origins (O_A, O_B) exist because readers disagreed on five origin levels. Claim outcome at the origin = the common outcome if O_A and O_B agree; if they differ, the claim is label-sensitive and its outcome is indeterminate (origin_label_sensitive), with both reported.
discrepancy_across_readings: scoring.md requires discrepancy at the origin and at every equivalent reading. The substantive equivalent set is empty (only algebraic checks), so the condition is discrepant_candidate at both origins O_A and O_B. Uncertain-set results are reported as context and, if any uncertain reading is consistent, the claim is flagged label-sensitive and becomes indeterminate (label_sensitive) rather than discrepant.
fragility: Specification fragility requires a substantive equivalent set; it is empty here, so fragility is 'not assessed'. Uncertain-set dispersion (sign share, share significant at .05 in the hypothesised direction, median, min-max, position of published estimate) is reported separately.

multiverse_summary_rules.sign_share: share of ok uncertain specs with the published sign
multiverse_summary_rules.significance_share: share with two-sided p<.05 and the hypothesised sign
multiverse_summary_rules.dedupe: identical sample_hash and identical estimates counted once; algebraic checks excluded

precedence: discrepant (only after adversarial review and human confirmation; otherwise reported as discrepant_candidate -> formal outcome indeterminate (pending_confirmation))
descriptives: Table 1 means/SDs/correlations compared on rounding intervals only, reported descriptively (no SE): agreement if within the printed precision interval widened by 10% relative; informational, does not drive the paper outcome.
f_tests: Compare significance (published text p<.001 for all three; reconstructed upper-tail p) and report F values; magnitude not audited.
failure_policy: Failed or unavailable specs are listed and never counted as agreement or disagreement.
compute_budget: per grid_v1.json; exceeding it stops further runs and is reported.
adversarial_review: Required for any discrepant_candidate. No model family independent of both implementer families is available; any discrepant claim is reported as not fully verified.
